- When sentiment is bullish (≥0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >10% from prior day), model often overshoots and fails to correct — apply downward bias correction after peak.
- If supply net is negative and events are frequent, model overconfidently assumes price stability — adjust downward by 2–5% for 30d horizon.
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and supply net is negative, model underestimates downside risk — add 3–7% downward buffer in forecast.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is rising steadily, true outcome often reverses mid-horizon — cap upward trend at 3–5% above recent 7d average.
- For 30d forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, reduce forecast by 1–3% per event beyond 15 events — adjust linearly with event density.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model fails to capture volatility — apply volatility-adjusted smoothing (e.g., ±2% band around 7d moving avg).
